# Sandlock

> Sandlock is a lightweight Linux process sandbox that confines untrusted code with Landlock, seccomp-bpf, and seccomp user notification. It applies a kernel-enforced policy to a process before it executes, with no root, no container image, no container runtime, and no hypervisor. Startup overhead is about 5 ms. Apache-2.0, written in Rust, maintained by Multikernel Technologies.

Sandlock is built for code you did not write: AI agent tool calls, untrusted CI builds, per-request code execution, and function-as-a-service. Every path, network destination, and syscall is denied unless the policy allows it. Static rules are enforced by the kernel; a small userspace supervisor handles runtime decisions such as destination IP checks, HTTP method and path rules, credential injection, copy-on-write writes, and resource limits, all without cgroups or namespaces.

Requirements: Linux 6.12 or later by default (older kernels can waive individual protections). Sandlock is a process sandbox, not a VM: it shares the host kernel and is not the right tool when a separate kernel is required.

## Start here

- [Getting Started](https://sandlock.io/docs/getting-started.html): install, check the kernel, run a first confined command
- [How Sandlock Works](https://sandlock.io/how-it-works.html): Landlock, seccomp-bpf, seccomp notify, and the supervisor
- [Security Model](https://sandlock.io/security.html): trust boundaries, guarantees per layer, what is out of scope
- [Comparison](https://sandlock.io/comparison.html): Sandlock vs containers, microVMs, gVisor, bubblewrap, and when it is the wrong tool
- [Use Cases](https://sandlock.io/use-cases.html): AI agents, CI, per-request execution, FaaS, Kubernetes
- [FAQ](https://sandlock.io/faq.html): running inside Docker, the pidfd_getfd seccomp gate, CAP_SYS_PTRACE
